headline.text: L1 S2 enrober belt *ripped during production* — line stopped and cleaned, but no product hold or QA disposition documented in window.

summary: One high-severity event: L1 S2 enrober belt failed during production run with potential for belt material contamination; line cleaned and belt replacement scheduled Monday. L3 ML1 caught belt fraying during startup before depositing. L2 ML2 mold cooler filters out for washing, awaiting reinstallation.

food_safety.title: Enrober belt ripped during production run
food_safety.summary: S2 enrober belt ripped at 21:39 during active production; line stopped immediately and full cleaning performed with ATP pass, but no product hold or QA review of at-risk product documented in window.
food_safety.status: Line cleaned and shut down; C&E scheduled for belt replacement Monday 07:30; no mention of product disposition.

food_safety.title: ML1 C6 belt fraying caught during startup
food_safety.summary: Belt fraying with loose fibers detected at 22:50 during startup sequence before depositing began; maintenance torched belt to secure frays.
food_safety.status: Resolved during shift — belt torched, maintenance addressed multiple belt issues overnight, line eventually resumed.

quality.title: ML2 mold cooler filters removed, awaiting reinstallation
quality.summary: Cooler filters pulled for washing at shift end; filters must be reinstalled before line can run.
quality.status: Open — filters drying, not yet reinstalled; supervisor flagged for completion before startup.

sanitation.title: S2 post-shutdown cleaning verification passed
sanitation.summary: Full line cleaning following belt failure verified by ATP; all tunnels, melting tank, and equipment passed at shift end.
sanitation.status: Resolved — ATP pass confirmed 03:20, crew released.

sanitation.title: ML1 cleaning verifications during troubled startup
sanitation.summary: Multiple ATP checks (dosings, plate, rollers) all passed during night of repeated mechanical issues and line stops.
sanitation.status: Resolved — all sanitation checks passed despite multiple equipment teardowns.

opportunities.text: Consider adding explicit product-hold step to equipment-failure response checklist — based on S2 belt rip during production with no QA disposition documented in window.
Consider adding conveyor-belt fraying inspection to ML1 startup checklist — based on C6 belt fraying caught during warmup, echoing recurring belt wear patterns.
